objections.claim_attacked: post_state — 'GRT was reported to complete ('could finish GRT', 'complete BoomTile') after reducing the layer adjustment to 0.2 and setting congestion iterations to 35. No re-measured DRC count was given.'
objections.objection: The record's own text does not establish that 20k congestion DRCs were eliminated or even reduced; it only asserts GRT 'could finish' / 'complete BoomTile'. Completion of GRT is not the same as clearing the observed 20k routing congestion DRCs, and the episode does not report a post-fix DRC count, so the causal outcome claimed in chosen_intervention is not measured in the record.

objections.claim_attacked: hypothesis — 'The GRT routing-layer adjustment of 0.45 (originally derived from other asap7 designs) is too aggressive for this design; the default 30 congestion iterations were also insufficient.'
objections.objection: The record supports that 0.45 was used and that reducing it to 0.2 plus increasing iterations to 35 was tried, but it does not contain evidence isolating which lever mattered, whether the two changes were confounded, or whether the change fixes congestion versus merely allowing GRT to proceed. That makes the stated hypothesis plausible but not confirmed by this record.

objections.claim_attacked: chosen_intervention — attributed causal fix: layer adjustment 0.45 -> 0.2 and congestion iterations 30 -> 35
objections.objection: Attribution_check passes for the direct_quote text and its by/date/locator, but the quote itself is a 'we could finish GRT by...' proposal; the record does not clearly show that the same participant later confirmed the change was applied and produced the reported completion, nor whether completion was on the same run/revision.

mechanism_check: Plausible but not tight: a lower routing-layer adjustment can make global routing less optimistic about available track resources and reduce reported congestion/overflow, and more congestion iterations can converge further; together they can let GRT complete. The break is that the record does not show the congestion DRCs dropping from ~20k, so the mechanism is not shown to explain the observed congestion — only to explain 'GRT could finish'.
evidence_check: Not measured: post_state is asserted, not quantified. What was actually reported: verbal completion ('could finish GRT', 'complete BoomTile') with no post-fix DRC count, no runtime, and no confirmation that congestion DRCs were reduced. A closed-out fix here would have to show at least a post-fix DRC/overflow count and ideally whether the macro-loop behavior changed.
attribution_check: Sound on its face: direct_quote is attributed to eder-matheus with date 2024-11-14 and locator to issue #6066, and its text supports the layer-adjustment change claim. The attribution does not, by itself, establish that the quoted proposal is what produced the reported completion.
missing_from_story: Whether the fix was actually merged as a code/configuration change and in what form (PR, commit, or local/ad-hoc parameter change)
A post-fix congestion/DRC measurement and whether the top-of-die and macro-region congestion persisted
Whether the macro-looping path issue (#5971) was actually addressed or only deferred
Whether the change was a tooling parameter tuned locally or a design-flow recommendation
Any indication of repeatability — one successful run versus a stable fix
most_defensible_part: The observation and candidates_considered fields: '20k routing congestion DRCs at 0.24 placement density with a top-of-die/macro congestion region' and the enumerated candidate interventions are internally consistent with the record and are the part I would keep unchanged.
